instruction: Enable automatic screen lock and set the screen to go blank after 10 minutes of inactivity.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated Settings → Privacy → Screen, enabled Automatic Screen Lock toggle, and set Blank Screen Delay to 5 minutes in 9 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate GNOME Settings panels, toggle switches on/off, use dropdown menus, understand privacy/screen lock settings.
metadata.task_rationale: Harder variation of the original task. Requires both enabling screen lock AND setting a specific blank delay (10 minutes instead of the 5 minutes the model chose). Tests precise dropdown selection.
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling automatic screen lock and setting idle delay to 10 minutes. Custom getter reads both gsettings values. Metric gives 0.5 partial credit for each correct setting.

scoring_breakdown.idle_delay: 0.5 - Blank screen delay set to 10 minutes (uint32 600)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads both relevant gsettings keys: org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay and org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled
Expected values are semantically correct: 600 seconds = 10 minutes for idle delay, 'true' for lock enabled
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter for type='rule' by directly accessing expected.get('expected_idle_delay') without unwrapping a 'rules' key
Both instruction requirements (enable screen lock + set 10 min blank delay) are fully covered with appropriate 0.5 partial credit each
No postconfig needed since getter reads gsettings via command line, not UI state
Config correctly sets lock-enabled to false as initial state, ensuring the task has something to verify
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: idle_delay check uses substring match ('600' in 'uint32 600') which could theoretically match values like 6000 or 16005. Consider using a regex or splitting the output to extract the numeric value for exact comparison. This is a very low-risk issue since standard GNOME idle-delay values don't cause false matches.
